description:
Episode 33 of a daily journey through the universe. 🌠
Tonight (Dec 13–14) the Geminid meteor shower peaks: up to 120 meteors an hour under dark skies, a thin crescent Moon that sets early, and shooting stars that come from an asteroid. How and when to watch.

segments.text: Episode thirty-three. Next stop... tonight's shooting stars.
Tonight, the Geminid meteor shower peaks. It's the strongest shower of the year.
segments.headline: Peaks tonight

segments.text: Under a dark sky, you could see up to about a hundred twenty shooting stars an hour.
And this year the Moon is only a thin crescent that sets early, so the sky will stay dark.
segments.headline: Dark skies this year

segments.text: Most meteor showers come from comets. The Geminids come from an asteroid, called thirty-two hundred Phaethon.
segments.headline: They come from an asteroid

segments.text: They hit our atmosphere at about thirty-five kilometers per second, and burn up.
Best time: after midnight. Find a dark place, let your eyes adjust, and look up. No telescope needed.
segments.headline: How to watch
